(a) credal self-supervision outperforms state-of-the-art methods in the low-data regime; (b) the proposed approach is able to learn in the presence of high uncertainty and to represent this uncertainty in a more flexible manner than existing self-supervised methods; (c) credal self-training can be applied to any self-supervision method and is thus a generalization of existing approaches; and (d) the proposed methodology is applicable to a wide range of learning tasks,
